ACM has gone from laggard to leader: +19.69% over one month against SPY -3.62% and XLI -0.25%, the strongest 1-month relative move in the open book, and it is doing it on infrastructure and water backlog rather than on the AI-capex narrative that is currently de-rating — SMH is -18.17% over the same month. The reason to keep holding rather than ring the register now is the Q4 print, which is the first dated test of that backlog conversion; the reason to trim half before it is that the move has already happened.
key_risk: ACM reported actual EPS of -0.50 against a 1.4809 estimate for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, a 133.8% miss, so this management has shown it can lose control of a quarter. Running 12% above the SMA20 into that print is the setup where a disappointment gaps straight through the 61.50 stop rather than trading down to it. Compounding it, the print date is not company-confirmed — 11-16 after the close per two calendars, 11-17 estimated per a third, and AECOM has historically released Q4 before the open — so anyone planning to trim on the morning after a presumed 11-16 close could be trimming after the gap. Be flat the half by the 11-16 close.
counter_argument: Analyst revisions are deteriorating, not improving: bullish share has fallen from 83.3% in August to 76.5% in November (-6.8pp), with buy ratings cut from 11 to 9 while holds rose. So the sell side is getting less positive exactly as the price gets more positive, and the target of 77.22 sits above the 120-day range high of 76.85 — it requires a breakout to new highs, not a continuation inside the range. That target is inherited from the original publication and is deliberately not revised upward here; the trim instruction is what takes money off instead.
